acceptanceCriteria: Every clickable architecture element (agents, entrySurface, contract, runtime, repository, repositoryProtocol, evidence, knowledge, outcome, humanControlInterface, humanAuthority, workItem) shows a pointer cursor on hover via useCursor and a subtle hover-state visual change distinct from its selected and dimmed states.

Hover state does not persist or apply to dimmed elements in a way that implies they are interactable when they are not the current focus, and hover produces no continuous per-frame animation loop -- it is a discrete on/off state change.

The Work Item panel, Verification panel, and Overview detail block fade in over a short duration on mode or selection change instead of appearing instantly, using the existing motion token scale rather than inventing new arbitrary durations.
prefers-reduced-motion results in an instant appearance with no fade, matching the existing reduced-motion discipline used everywhere else in this codebase.
npm ci, lint, typecheck, unit tests, Playwright e2e, and the static export build all succeed with no regression to any prior WI's established acceptance behavior.
goal: Ship v0.2.5: every clickable 3D architecture element shows a pointer cursor and a subtle hover highlight (distinct from selected/dimmed state) via drei's useCursor and local pointer-over/out state, and the mode-specific DOM panels (Work Item, Verification, Overview detail block) fade in smoothly on mode/selection change instead of appearing with a hard cut, respecting prefers-reduced-motion by skipping the fade.
intent: The user confirmed the information/layout issues (label overlap, panel occlusion) are resolved and asked for further visual improvement suggestions. The agreed next step is small, low-risk interaction polish rather than more material/lighting work: hover affordance on clickable 3D elements, and smoother DOM panel transitions when switching modes.
